title: Feedback that changes behaviour, not just feelings
performance: Before giving a piece of feedback, the viewer can restate a verdict about the person as one specific, observed behaviour, its concrete impact, and a question that ends in an agreed next step

audience.assumed_prior: has given and received everyday feedback at work; senses that 'be more proactive' style comments rarely change anything, but has not named why
audience.why: the brief targets corporate employees who already give feedback to peers or people they lead, not newcomers learning what feedback is
audience.motivation: assigned or chosen short L&D viewing; moderate investment, rewarded if their next awkward conversation actually works
audience.context: desk or phone, sound likely on, captions available, one sitting of about two minutes

strategy.name: worked_example_led
strategy.rationale: one running moment (a deliverable flagged late on the due day) shows the verdict failing first; the shape is then built on that same moment, so each part is seen doing work before it is named
strategy.signature_move: replay the same moment and swap the verdict for one piece of the shape at a time: the behaviour, then the impact, then the question and next step

misconceptions.belief: if I say the problem clearly and firmly, the person will do it differently next time
misconceptions.why_tempting: the receiver reacts at once (nods, apologises, looks uncomfortable), so the feedback looks like it landed
misconceptions.source_anchor: knowledge sheet F5, F6 (person-directed feedback triggers defensiveness; vague feedback names no action to repeat or stop)

hook.sketch: Say a teammate tells you on the due day that the report will be late. You say 'you need to be more proactive'. They nod and feel bad. Two weeks later, same day, same message.

arc.promise: You can turn that one sentence into feedback they can actually act on next time
arc.bridge_from_prior: sec1 opens from the 'be more proactive' line the viewer has almost certainly said or heard

sections.goal: the viewer can explain the difference between a trait label ('not proactive') and a specific, observed behaviour ('told me on Thursday, the due day')
concepts: why a label changes feelings, not actions

sections.goal: the viewer can use the shape on the same moment: add the concrete impact, then close with a question that hears their side and agrees one next step
the viewer can distinguish which of two lines about the same moment gives the teammate something to do differently
concepts: behaviour, impact, question, next step (in order)

arc.payoff: Back to the opening moment, now with the shape: the teammate suggests flagging any slip by the midpoint, and next time the warning comes early

practice_ladder.what: the late deliverable rebuilt step by step, each part of the shape narrated as it is added
two lines about the same late deliverable; the viewer picks before the narrator answers
the viewer is handed their own next 'be more X' sentence to rebuild

slowdown_at: the closing question and agreed next step

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: Same late report, two lines: 'You need to be more proactive' versus 'You told me about the delay on Thursday, the due day, and I had to move the client call. What would help you flag it sooner?' Which one gives them something to do differently?
recall_moments.answer: The second: it names the behaviour and its impact, and opens a next step
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: the first feels honest and direct, and the person reacts at once, but reacting is not knowing what to change

transfer_tasks: The next time you are about to say someone should 'be more' something, name what they did and when, what it affected, then ask what would help next time

persona.voice: a mentor who has given plenty of feedback that did not land before learning the shape; plain, warm, direct, a colleague not a coach
persona.delivery_notes: light and knowing on the hook, matter of fact on each part of the shape, slower and curious on the question, brisk on the close

gagne.attention: hook: the late report and the 'be more proactive' line that changed nothing
gagne.objective: promise: turn that one sentence into feedback they can act on
gagne.recall_prior: bridge_from_prior: the viewer's own 'be more proactive' line
gagne.present: sec1 behaviour vs trait, then sec2 impact and question, in dependency order
gagne.guidance: signature_move: the same moment rebuilt one part at a time
gagne.practice: practice_ladder; the faded step is the sec3 check
gagne.feedback: the check answer explains why the tempting first line fails
gagne.assess: sec3 check: choose before the answer
gagne.transfer: transfer_tasks: the viewer's own next 'be more X' sentence

merrill.problem_centered: the late deliverable is the running problem throughout
merrill.demonstration: sec1-sec2 rebuild the moment step by step

mayer.coherence: one running example; no tour of other techniques
mayer.signalling: one slowdown on the question and next step
mayer.redundancy: on screen holds short labels and the two lines only; narration explains
mayer.contiguity: each part appears as it is spoken
mayer.segmenting: three short sections, one idea each
mayer.pre_training: sec1 names behaviour vs trait before sec2 builds on it

arcs.attention: the same late message arriving twice
arcs.relevance: the viewer's own next feedback conversation
arcs.confidence: the shape is modelled before the check asks them to choose
arcs.satisfaction: the payoff shows the warning arrive early
